title: Integer `//` has no domain error
verdict: every input is in the domain; zero divisors and `MIN // -1` are other options
description: Integer floor division gives a quotient for every pair of operands but two kinds: a zero divisor is NULL (`on_division_by_zero`) and `MIN // -1` wraps to `MIN` (`overflow`), both in polars-int-divide. No input raises or gives a value of its own. The kernels are one macro for `Int8` to `Int64`. `/` on integers divides doubles (polars-int-true-divide).
reference: `divide` on integers: `on_domain_error` never applies (`int.div` in docs/core-semantics.md, `Choice.any`).

evidence.note: Column by column: a zero divisor is masked to NULL, the rest is `wrapping_floor_div_mod`.
A literal divisor: 0 gives NULL, -1 negates (wrapping), others divide the absolute values.

notes: One macro instantiates the integer kernels for i8 to i64, so the reading covers every width. Each path handles a zero divisor and `MIN // -1` and returns a quotient for every other input.
Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3). The streaming engine evaluates expressions through polars-expr on each morsel (crates/polars-stream/src/expression.rs), so these kernels serve both engines.

evidence.note: Rust `test_signed_wrapping_div_mod`: for every `i8` pair, `wrapping_floor_div_mod` equals the floor quotient and remainder of the doubles, wrapped to `i8` (`(x as i32) as i8`), and (0, 0) for a zero divisor. So `-128 // -1` is -128, `-128 % -1` is 0, and no pair panics.
`test_floordiv_mod`: `lit(1, Int8) // lit(0, Int8)` and `%` are NULL, as for the default `Int32` literals; 10 // 3 is 3. Eager `pl.select`, in memory
`test_truncdiv_int` (Int8, lazy `collect()`): `truncdiv` gives -128 for -128 / -1 and NULL for 5 / 0; its comment says `floordiv` does the same

notes: The Rust test shows the floor-division kernel gives a value for every `Int8` pair (the zero divisor's (0, 0) is masked to NULL by the caller), so no `Int8` input raises. `test_floordiv_mod` pins NULL for a zero divisor at `Int8` and `Int32`. `i16` and `i64` rest on the source reading of the shared macro.

Polars's CI runs the unit tests by default, where a lazy `collect()` without `engine` runs the streaming engine (also once with `POLARS_IDEAL_MORSEL_SIZE=4`), and again with `POLARS_ENGINE_AFFINITY=in-memory` (.github/workflows/test-python.yml#L55-L78, #L168-L178); eager `Series` and `DataFrame` calls run in memory. Read at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), not run.
